overall: The AG found the Runkle School Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law at its March 7, 2013 meeting on any of the five allegations; the recording-announcement claim was unresolved for lack of evidence, and no order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 7, 2013 meeting was not open to the public because a no-trespass order barred him from attending the school where it was held.
allegations.key_passage: That the Complainant personally could not attend the meeting because a No Trespass Order prohibited him from attending does not mean that the meeting was closed to the public.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the council failed to announce at the meeting's start that his son was video recording. The council said the chair made the announcement, which the minutes omit.
allegations.key_passage: Because we have not been presented with evidence to support either version of the events that occurred, we are unable to resolve this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 7, 2013 minutes were inadequate and inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes of the Council's March 7, 2013 meeting provide enough detail of the proceeding such that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have a clear understanding of what occurred.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes did not list documents and exhibits used at the March 7, 2013 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Council complied with the law's requirements in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the council failed to post its March 7, 2013 minutes online within ten days of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: There is no requirement that meeting minutes be posted online at all, let alone within ten days of the meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
